answer: At each summit of the network cycle, every agent must solve a crystal‑structured proof that ties its identity to a unique delta of recent state transitions, forcing it to produce a fresh reasoning trace that only the genuine model can generate. The verifier checks the trace against the latest state graph; any replica that cannot recompute the delta is rejected. An attacker therefore pays full model‑inference cost for each fake identity per epoch, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
